t:
(a) Notification of Issuance.—Section 1567a of title 10, United States Code, is amended—
        (1) in subsection (a), by striking “and any individual involved in the order does not reside on a military installation at any time during the duration of the military protective order, the commander of the military installation shall notify” and inserting “, the commander of the unit to which the member is assigned shall, not later than seven days after the date of the issuance of the order, notify”; 
        (2) by redesignating subsection (b) as subsection (c); 
        (3) by inserting after subsection (a) the following new subsection (b);“(b) Notification in Event of Transfer.—In the event that a member of the armed forces against whom a military protective order is issued is transferred to another unit—“(1) not later than the date of the transfer, the commander of the unit from which the member is transferred shall notify the commander of the unit to which the member is transferred of—“(A) the issuance of the protective order; and“(B) the individuals involved in the order; and“(2) not later than seven days after receiving the notice under paragraph (1), the commander of the unit to which the member is transferred shall provide notice of the order to the appropriate civilian authorities in accordance with subsection (a).”; and 
        (4) in subsection (c), as so redesignated, by striking “commander of the military installation” and inserting “commander of the unit to which the member is assigned”.  
    (b) Annual Report Required.—Not later than March 1, 2021, and each year thereafter through 2025, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report that identifies—
        (1) the number of military protective orders issued in the calendar year preceding the year in which the report is submitted; and 
        (2) the number of such orders that were reported to appropriate civilian authorities in accordance with section 1567a(a) of title 10, United States Code, in such preceding year.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that notifying "appropriate civilian authorities" is coordination with outside (state or local) entities. But this is a one-way notice sent after a military protective order has already been issued; the civilian authorities are not consulted and have no input into any federal decision. The other elements are notice between unit commanders and an annual report to the congressional defense committees, both of which stay inside the federal government.
fable.s: the commander of the unit to which the member is transferred shall provide notice of the order to the appropriate civilian authorities in accordance with subsection (a)

qwen_block.w: The section describes internal notifications between military commanders and a report to Congress. Congress is inside the federal government, and military commanders are federal officials. There is no consultation with or participation by outside parties (such as the public, states, or non-federal entities) in any decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report

opus.w: The section requires commanders to notify civilian authorities after a protective order has already been issued. That is a one-way notice, not consultation or coordination before a federal decision. The other duties are notices between military commanders and a report to the congressional defense committees, and all of those stay inside the federal government. Even though civilian authorities are outside parties, they have no role in the decision, so this is not participation.
opus.s: not later than seven days after receiving the notice under paragraph (1), the commander of the unit to which the member is transferred shall provide notice of the order to the appropriate civilian authorities in accordance with subsection (a).
opus.b:
1. **The tempting reading:** Commanders must notify "appropriate civilian authorities," which are outside the federal government. It's easy to read that as outside involvement in a federal decision.
2. **Why it fails:** The notice goes one way and comes after the military protective order has already been issued. The civilian authorities have no part in making the decision. The other duties are commander-to-commander notices and an annual report to the congressional defense committees, and both stay inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires military commanders to notify civilian authorities after a protective order is issued. This is a post-decision notification, not a consultation or coordination with outside parties before a federal decision is made. The other interactions involve military commanders (inside the government) or reports to Congress (inside the government). Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: the commander of the unit to which the member is transferred shall provide notice of the order to the appropriate civilian authorities in accordance with subsection (a)
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that notifying "appropriate civilian authorities" constitutes coordination with outside entities. However, the definition explicitly excludes mere notifications or reports to outside parties if they are not part of a consultative process *before* a decision is made. Here, the notification is a post-decision administrative requirement (informing civilians that an order exists), not a mechanism for civilians to influence the issuance of the order. Furthermore, the other interactions described are between military commanders (inside the government) or reports to Congress (inside the government).
